note: Slide-title grammar (Plan §13). Observed distribution across 116 real content-slide titles: ~52 topic, ~43 descriptive, ~21 takeaway. CORRECTION to earlier guidance: most IM titles are topic or descriptive LABELS, not full-sentence takeaways. Reserve takeaway titles for market/positioning/strategy arguments where the page proves a claim. Title font is Merriweather serif, sentence case (never Title Case).

topic.when: Standard content, product, operations, financial-statement pages where the title just names the subject.

descriptive.when: Add one qualifying adjective the page then supports.

takeaway.when: Market, positioning, customer and strategy slides that argue a full claim the body proves.
examples: Healthcare demand in the Benelux is structurally growing
BeMedico is perfectly positioned in the right core end-markets
European legislation is driven by the Medical Device Regulation (MDR)
Highly diversified customer base with limited customer dependency
Recurring revenue is the key driver for growth over the historical period
Fragmented market with Irmaco as a unique one-stop-shop

financial.when: Financial-statement / QoE pages — a formal statement label, often with a prefix.

conventions.case: Sentence case, serif (Merriweather). Never Title Case.
conventions.multipart: Split a long section across pages with (1/2)/(2/2) suffixes, or run one sentence across slides with leading/trailing '...' (Torino: 'Strong focus on operational excellence ...' -> '... driven by best-in-class service and maintenance ...').
conventions.subtitle: An optional teal/muted serif subtitle under the title carries the one-line descriptor (e.g. 'Independent distributor of innovative products for medical professionals').
